entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Caedicius Noctua was a Roman politician and orator who rose to prominence in the late 4th century BC. Born into a plebeian family, he became known for his eloquence and persuasive abilities, which earned him a seat on the tribune of the plebs. He served as a consul in 345 BCE but was later exiled due to his involvement in a conspiracy against the Roman dictator, Servius Sulpicius Rufus.

As a member of the Second Triumvirate, Noctua played a key role in the First Triumvirate's efforts to defeat their common enemies, including the Pontic king Mithridates VI. He also contributed to the construction of several public buildings and roads during his time as consul.

Despite his significant contributions to Roman politics and infrastructure, Noctua's legacy was largely forgotten by the time of the Roman Empire's rise. However, he remains an important figure in understanding the complexities of late republican Rome and its transition to the imperial period.
